title: Sisters in Sweat
tagline: Building the brand strategy, voice and visual identity for a fitness community from the ground up.

image.alt: Sisters in Sweat brand strategy and campaigns

context: Sisters in Sweat had grown fast — a fitness and wellness community running large-scale events and partnering with brands like Cava, Nike, Mille, Nykaa Wellness and Zerodha — without a formal brand system behind any of it. Every collaboration, campaign and event was being built without a shared visual language or a documented way of working.
problem: Growing this quickly without structure carried real risk: brand collaborations could look inconsistent from one partner to the next, there was no shared reference for how the brand should look or sound, and day-to-day operations — meeting cadence, documentation, admin — were eating time that should have gone into the work itself. Building the brand system in-house also meant avoiding the cost of hiring an external branding agency.
process: Owned the rebranding project end-to-end, single-handedly delivering a full brand guideline deck covering strategy, visual identity and design mock-ups. Built the brand-led marketing charter that now guides every collaboration, from Cava and Nike to Mille, Nykaa Wellness and In Her Interest by Zerodha. Set up systems and clearer lines of communication while managing a 4-person team alongside the co-founder, along with trackers and documentation that cut down time spent on meetings and repetitive admin work. Led creative direction for brand collaboration shoots (Cava, Akshayakalpa, Liquid IV), owned content strategy including a full Instagram revamp and Meta ads, and personally shot and edited ad videos. Ran social media campaigns end-to-end for flagship community IPs — Sweat Fest, The Sistra Run, and the Nike x SIS Cricket Tournament — and helped shape the personal brand of co-founder Swetha Subbiah.
outcome: Sisters in Sweat now runs on a brand system built entirely in-house, at zero agency cost — one consistent visual identity across every partner collaboration, clearer systems that free up the team's time, and flagship events carrying a unified brand voice from first announcement to final post.

title: Mohmani
tagline: Creative strategy for an up-and-coming homegrown jewellery brand.

image.alt: Mohmani Instagram grid and brand world

context: Mohmani is a small, homegrown jewellery label that specialises in one-of-one pieces and custom orders. Over time, it has grown into a content and culture-heavy brand, shaped as much by the founder's personal voice as by the jewellery itself. Through viral content, events and word-of-mouth discovery, the brand has built a niche following of around 3.3k people who connect with its whimsical world.
problem: As Mohmani became more visible, the challenge wasn't reach — it was coherence. With the brand evolving across content, pop-ups and personal brand, there was a real risk of it feeling scattered or performative. The need was for clearer creative direction that could hold all of this together, without forcing the brand into a conventional lifestyle or commercial mould.
process: The focus was on putting some structure in place so creative decisions didn't feel random. Early on, the brand's core cues — whimsy, quirk, and subcultural references — were clearly defined and used to guide everything. Basic direction was set for visuals, tone, and a content calendar so posting stayed consistent and intentional. Each collection started with a clear inspiration, which was shared with the audience through creative concepts and content instead of long explanations. Content pillars were built around the jewellery itself, the making process, everyday moments, and the founder's personal voice, so the brand felt natural and expressive rather than over-produced. Over time, engagement, pop-ups, and viral moments were looked at to understand what resonated and refine the direction while staying true to the brand's niche.
outcome: Mohmani now feels more settled in its identity — less like a brand chasing growth, and more like one that has found its place. The creative strategy helped bring clarity and continuity across content, community moments, and product storytelling, while keeping the brand's quirks intact. It also gave the founder a flexible framework to keep experimenting, growing, and showing up authentically without losing what makes the brand resonate.
